question: How many states in India have a bicameral legislature?
solution:
The correct answer is __6.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bicameral structure means having both a Lower and Upper house, which mimics the structure of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha as- 

 
 
• Legislative Assembly/Vidhan Sabha. 
 
• Legislative Council/Vidhan Parishad.
 
 
 
• 
 
Currently, 6 states in India have a bicameral structure, which are

 
 
• 
 
Andhra Pradesh, 

 
 
• 
 
Uttar Pradesh, 

 
 
• 
 
Bihar, 

 
 
• 
 
Maharashtra,

 
 
• 
 
Karnataka and

 
 
• 
 
Telangana

 
 
 
 
• 
 
The remaining 22 states have a unicameral structure, which means they have only the Legislative Assembly and not the Legislative Council. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
State legislature: 

 
 
• 
 
A state legislature is a legislative branch or body of a political subdivision in a federal system. For every state, there is a legislature, which consists of the Governor and one house or two houses.

 
 
 
 
• Articles 168 to 177: 
 
 
• "Deals with Constitution of Legislatures in States"- Article 168.
 
• "Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States"- Article 169.
 
• "Composition of the Legislative Assemblies"- Article 170.
 
• "To become a member of the state legislature"- Article 173.
